```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE,comment="#>")
library(gof)
path <- system.file("extdata","fixed-order","summary.csv",package="gof")
evidence <- read.csv(path,stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(evidence)==106L,sum(evidence$primary_family)==16L,
          all(evidence$definite_rejections<=evidence$possible_rejections),
          all(rowSums(evidence[paste0("count_",c("R","N","U","OF","DG","IN"))])==evidence$N))
percent <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f%%",100*x)
display <- function(d) data.frame(
  scenario=d$scenario,test=d$statistic,N=d$N,
  definite=percent(d$definite_rate),possible=percent(d$possible_rate),
  completion_interval=paste0("[",percent(d$lower95),", ",percent(d$upper95),"]"),
  check.names=FALSE)
```

## What was assessed

The November 2026 study assessed the existing response bootstrap at declared
Poisson/log and binomial/logit design/parameter points. It retained **637,000
records and 106 cells**: 15 null scenarios with fitted bootstrap, legacy
multiplier and specified-null arms, plus eight power alternatives.

Eight primary null scenarios each used **N=20,000** outer samples and **B=999**
inner requests. Every ordering was fixed independently of the response;
`subset.max=Inf` and `b=0` were used. Bootstrap refits retained the design,
offsets, binomial trials and declared fitting controls. Early stopping was
allowed only after both rejection decisions were determined. Audit prefixes
and every power sample executed the full inner simulation count. Statistic
matrices were retained for fitted-null primary prefixes; control/power matrices
were not stored. All attempts retain counts and RNG-state hashes. This limits
post hoc trajectory inspection and is disclosed alongside the full-count checks.

The study does not qualify fitted ordering, the default capped grid when
n>500, moving windows, overdispersion, clustered units or arbitrary links.
It is evidence at the declared points, not uniform control over composite
nulls or a proof of an asymptotic theorem. Its derived full-grid argument
remains distinct from empirical measurement.

The assessment was **model-assisted, without independent human review**, under
an explicit owner decision replacing the external-review requirement. The
**4–6% practical criterion is project-specific**, not a universal statistical
standard or exact nominal 5% control. Code and design were frozen before the
fresh confirmation samples; prior development evidence had been seen.

## Failure accounting and uncertainty

Every planned sample remains in the denominator. R denotes definite rejection,
N definite non-rejection, U unresolved tail completion, OF outer failure,
DG a degenerate/noninformative process and IN indeterminate information.
Let D count R and E count R+U+OF+IN. The interval [D/N,E/N] describes unresolved
completion; it is not a sampling confidence interval.

The displayed **pointwise 95% completion interval** uses a lower exact binomial
limit for D and an upper limit for E, retaining both sampling and completion
uncertainty. It does not provide simultaneous coverage for every displayed
cell. A DG sample is not evidence that a diagnostic is calibrated; the
declared degeneracy/availability restrictions remain explicit project choices.

The primary assessment is a separate 16-cell family: eight scenarios by Sup
and L2 for fitted bootstrap. One-sided limits use tail .05/16 and an
intersection-union rule. At N=20,000, within-band support requires D>=878 and
E<=1108. P01 was predeclared upper-only. The family error statement concerns
false primary support promotions, not every displayed endpoint/classification.
The stricter 4.5–5.5% assessment is supplementary and descriptive.

## Primary findings

All **14 eligible primary cells** met the practical 4–6% rule. Both P01 cells
met only their predeclared upper-rate criterion; P01 is not an equivalence or
within-band result. Estimates and completion uncertainty remain visible:

```{r primary, results='asis'}
primary <- evidence[evidence$primary_family,]
knitr::kable(display(primary),row.names=FALSE)
```

These results do not show that the true rate is exactly .05 or close within
half a percentage point. In particular, B01 L2 has an observed rate of 5.44%.
The primary support conclusion uses the declared practical criterion, not
an interval merely containing .05.

## Controls and comparison

All **90 prespecified upper-alarm checks** on the specified-null arm remained
below their thresholds. That control requires genuinely specified means and
the independent response law. No lower-tail alarm was used: discrete
conservatism is permitted. Lack of an alarm is not a new simultaneous
calibration guarantee for every control cell.

```{r controls, results='asis'}
control <- evidence[evidence$study_role=="specified_control",]
knitr::kable(display(control),row.names=FALSE)
```

The legacy multiplier remains a separate asymptotic method. Its comparator
results are descriptive and are retained even when they are poor. The
bootstrap study does not qualify that comparator or justify choosing a
method after seeing the diagnostic outcomes.

```{r comparator, results='asis'}
comparator <- evidence[evidence$study_role=="multiplier_comparison",]
knitr::kable(display(comparator),row.names=FALSE)
```

## Stress cases and availability

The adverse findings are part of the evidence. P07 and B02 retain conservative
rates, failed fits and unresolved bounds. P08 had 1,521 degenerate samples
and 421 outer failures out of 2,000; it cannot establish fitted-null calibration.
L03's observed L2 rate is **6.62%**. It is a descriptive stress result, not a
primary qualification pass. Its pointwise interval and the full panel must be
considered; it does not establish a universal violation or identify a coding
defect by itself.

```{r stress, results='asis'}
stress <- evidence[evidence$study_role=="stress_calibration",]
knitr::kable(display(stress),row.names=FALSE)
```

Increasing nominal observations or exposure is not a universal adequacy rule.
No observed sample-size threshold, penalty, replacement fitter, rounding rule
or automatic method switch was selected to remove these outcomes. The separate
small-design guide explains leverage, sampling units and declared ordering.

## Power under the prespecified alternatives

Power rows report detection, not null calibration. Across the declared
alternatives the definite detection estimates range from 79.05% to 99.60%.
P01 retains a completion gap from failures/unresolved draws. These are
alternative-specific estimates with uncertainty, not a universal power claim
or a reason to select the better statistic after observing results.

```{r power, results='asis'}
power <- evidence[evidence$study_role=="power",]
knitr::kable(display(power),row.names=FALSE)
```

## Reuse and provenance

The compact evidence is installed and can be inspected without running a new
simulation:

```{r access}
files <- system.file("extdata","fixed-order",package="gof")
list.files(files)
evidence |> subset(primary_family,select=c(scenario,statistic,N,assessment))
```

`PROVENANCE.json` identifies the exact studied source/archive, protocol/harness
binding, confirmation seed and file hashes. `designs.rds` retains the null/power
design objects; `streams.rds` retains the frozen namespaces, including reserved
names, rather than the observed cohort data. The full all-attempt records and
frozen execution code remain in the project audit. The compact export is not
a standalone full execution archive.

A post-study audit verified all 6,370 chunks, 637,000 records, paired null
responses, counts, classifications, point values and 106 confidence summaries.
It also found a companion-harness metadata mismatch: legacy comparator k/B
points had plus-one inner completion bounds. Frozen records were preserved;
legacy point values, classifications, primary/control findings and the
count-based intervals above were unaffected. Future companion metadata is
corrected. This was not a change to package inference.

Review status, unresolved cases and finite-panel limits must accompany reused
results. The study does not replace the separate assumptions and approximate
calibration evidence for joint, ordinal or Gaussian SEM normality diagnostics.
